summary: Setting up a Calendly OAuth app is straightforward and can be completed directly through the developer portal. The main requirement is implementing the mandatory PKCE flow for all authorization requests.

approval.notes: The documentation does not explicitly state a review or approval process for new OAuth applications.

steps.title: Access Developer Portal
steps.detail: Navigate to the developer login page to manage your OAuth applications.

steps.title: Create OAuth App
steps.detail: On the OAuth apps tab, select Create OAuth app to register your integration.

steps.title: Configure App Details
steps.detail: Define your redirect URI and select the necessary scopes for your application's functionality.

nuances: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method.
Client secrets and webhook signing keys are only visible once during creation; they cannot be retrieved later.
Newly created OAuth apps require explicit scope requests to function.
agent_can_do: Draft the application name and description.
Generate the PKCE code verifier and code challenge for authorization requests.
Store the client ID and client secret in secure environment variables.
Construct the authorization URL with required parameters.
human_must_do: Log in to the Calendly developer portal.
Create the OAuth app in the dashboard.
Copy the client secret immediately upon creation as it cannot be viewed again.
Authorize the application during the initial testing phase.

create_app.quote: On the **OAuth apps** tab, select **Create OAuth app**.

credentials.quote: You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.

redirect_uri.quote: Redirect URI: the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app.

scopes.quote: Authorization scopes define the permissions that an application requests when accessing Calendly APIs on behalf of a user.

agent_human.quote: Until then, manage OAuth apps at [developer.calendly.com](https://developer.calendly.com/login).
